comparer_and_normalization_variants.finding: Every survivor-identity store is ordinal. Zero case-insensitive and zero culture-sensitive survivor-identity comparisons exist. The only real comparison defect is reference-equality dedupe in NeedsSystem/RadiationSystem, which permits duplicate ids rather than mis-comparing them.
comparer_and_normalization_variants.consequence_for_design: SurvivorId adopts ordinal equality with NO normalization. Because all 129 authored ids already match ^[a-z0-9_]+$, rejecting non-canonical input cannot break authored content, and over that value set OrdinalIgnoreCase and Ordinal are provably equivalent — so no comparer in the repo can disagree with SurvivorId.

id_grammar_evidence.conclusion: Survivor ids are snake_case with NO single mandatory prefix. A prefix check would reject 101 of 129 authored ids, so SurvivorId validates grammar only, never prefix.

definition_vs_entity.question: Phase 4 — are SurvivorDefinitionId and SurvivorId 1:1?
definition_vs_entity.evidence: SurvivorRosterSystem.Join(definitionId, day) sets survivorId = definitionId and refuses a second join for the same definition (_byId.ContainsKey guard). No code path generates a synthetic survivor.
definition_vs_entity.decision: Keep them as SEPARATE fields on the aggregate (SurvivorId + DefinitionId) but do not introduce a distinct SurvivorDefinitionId value type yet. The aggregate records the definition link so a future generated/duplicate survivor needs no identity migration, while today's data keeps DefinitionId == Id.Value.

discovered_defects.root_cause: NeedsSystem.Register and RadiationSystem.Register dedupe with List.Contains, i.e. reference equality. Neither system enforces per-Id uniqueness.
discovered_defects.mechanism: RestoreSave clears the host's RosterState and _radStates but never calls Needs.Unregister / Radiation.Unregister for the previously registered state objects. Fresh objects are appended; stale objects stay registered.
consequences: NeedsSystem.Get(id) returns the FIRST match, which is the STALE object — so SurvivorFateSystem.RunCascade's Get(id)/ForceDeath and the grief-morale loop mutate ghosts instead of live survivors
stale ghosts keep ticking and can reach 0 HP, firing OnDied -> OnSurvivorDied -> ReportDeath, killing a survivor who is alive in the loaded campaign
discovered_defects.status: confirmed by inspection; not yet fixed; scheduled with the Needs/Radiation migration (Phase 22/24) or as an isolated fix
discovered_defects.structural_fix: component stores keyed by SurvivorId with 0-or-1 cardinality make duplicate-id registration unrepresentable

discovered_defects.symptom: System.Collections.Generic.KeyNotFoundException: The given key 'survivor_a' was not present in the dictionary.
discovered_defects.mechanism: session.DispatchSortie("survivor_a", ...) does not produce an active sortie, so session.Engine.Active["survivor_a"] throws. Gates V1-V5 pass; V6 onward never run.
discovered_defects.second_defect: the harness prints EXPEDITION_SELFTEST PASS even though the gate throws, and the process then fails to exit (observed exit code 124 under timeout). A canonical CI gate can therefore report PASS while crashing, which means the 9 vehicle gates AGENTS.md claims are pinned are not actually all being exercised.
discovered_defects.provenance: PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by Task #132 P0. Verified by removing all six new Core files, rebuilding, and re-running the gate: the identical exception occurs. src/Host/HostCli.PanelTests.cs is unmodified since commit 4d1feb89.
discovered_defects.status: reported, not fixed — outside Task #132 scope (expedition vehicle logistics, Task #101)
discovered_defects.relevance_to_132: Phase 19 requires expedition participation to reconcile with survivor lifecycle. This gate must be green before the expedition domain can be migrated, because it is the contract that would detect a regression.
